tax.text:

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Net revenue generated from the Europe eCommerce distribution channel represented 6.8% of our total net revenue in Fiscal 2025.
located accounted for approximately 71% of our merchandise purchases in dollars.

In Fiscal 2025, our top 10 vendors accounted for approximately 63% of our merchandise purchases in dollars and we worked with approximately 40 vendors that manufactured substantially all of our products.
We also depend upon external vendors to print and mail our catalogs.
The success of our business depends on our overall marketing strategies for digital marketing and direct mail catalogs and customers’ use of our digital platform, including our eCommerce websites.
The success of our business depends on customers’ use of our eCommerce websites and their response to our digital marketing and direct mail catalogs.
As such, we rely on trademark and copyright law, trade secret protection and confidentiality agreements with our associates, consultants, vendors and others to protect our proprietary rights.

We rely on vendors to provide us with services in connection with certain aspects of our business, and any failure by these vendors to perform their obligations could have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.
We do not own or operate any significant manufacturing facilities and therefore depend upon independent merchandise suppliers and vendors for the manufacture of our merchandise.
We rely upon third-party land-based and air freight carriers for merchandise shipments from our distribution centers to customers.
Our own websites, third-party suppliers and third-party marketplaces rely on our ability to track and exchange accurate inventories by style, color and size to support customer orders.
Our success relies on maintaining good relations with these vendors.

Violation of ethical, labor, safety, or other standards by independent vendors and licensing partners, or the divergence of an independent vendor’s or licensing partner’s labor practices from those generally accepted as ethical in the United States could hurt our reputation or materially impact our ability to import products manufactured by these vendors or from the regions in which they operate, which could have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

We conduct business in and rely on sources for merchandise located in foreign markets and our business may therefore be adversely affected by legal, regulatory, economic and political risks associated with international trade in those markets.

Any inability on our part to successfully operate in foreign jurisdictions and rely on our foreign sources of production, due to any of the factors listed above, could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
We also rely on third‑party cloud hosting providers and software‑as‑a‑service platforms for critical parts of our infrastructure.
We also rely on third-party providers and platforms for some of these information technology systems and support.
We depend on the talents and continued efforts of our executive management team.

s.t: Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the MIPA, at closing (i) we will contribute all of our intellectual property and related assets associated with the “Lands’ End” brand, including all of the license agreements entered into in connection with Lands’ End’s licensing business to a newly formed Delaware limited liability company and wholly owned subsidiary of Lands’ End (“IPCo”), and (ii) immediately thereafter, we will sell a 50% controlling ownership stake in IPCo, to WHP for an aggregate purchase price of $300 million in cash.

Lands’ End’s licensing business (the “Contributed Assets”) to a newly formed Delaware limited liability company and wholly owned subsidiary of the Company (“IPCo”), and IPCo will assume certain liabilities related to the Contributed Assets and (ii) immediately thereafter, the Company will sell a 50 % controlling ownership stake in IPCo, to WHP for an aggregate purchase price of $ 300 million in cash (“the Transaction”).
In the event of such an exchange, our stake in IPCo would be valued at the EBITDA multiple implied by WHP Topco’s monetization event.

Additionally, in certain WHP Global monetization events, such as a qualifying public listing or majority sale, Lands’ End may have the right or obligation to exchange its interest in the joint venture for equity in WHP Global, at the same valuation multiple as the WHP monetization event.
The Company will account for its investment in IPCo under the equity method of accounting.
